current_upstream_source_audit.interpretation: CREST has a generic energy/gradient subprocess for ordinary calculator-driven workflows, but the current QCG source bypasses it: QCG constructs direct xTB single-point, optimization, and Hessian commands and accepts only GFN-family ensemble/frequency levels. The generic hook therefore does not establish an arbitrary-MLIP QCG free-energy backend.

febiss.interpretation: FEBISS converts a prior explicit-solvent trajectory and GIST site analysis into ranked solvent placements. Its voxel free-energy ranking is not the complete solute transfer free energy and cannot supply the missing pure-solvent, standard-state, coordination, or target-MLIP ensemble terms.

claim_scope: Primary-documentation and current-upstream-source audit of whether an automatic explicit-inner/implicit-outer workflow can presently produce neutral small-molecule absolute solvation free energies with arbitrary gas-phase MLIPs while preserving Route 1. This is not a QCG, FEBISS, or FreeSolv production run; it does not establish accuracy, speed, or generic MLIP compatibility.

current_route1_runtime.fixed_shell_definition: component membership and coordination number are fixed; coordinates remain task variables
current_route1_runtime.input: neutral closed-shell multicomponent MOL2 with fixed charges and explicit bonds
current_route1_runtime.interpretation: The existing runtime proves additive topology, energy, force, and MAPLE task plumbing for one illustrative prebuilt cluster. It does not compute an equilibrium shell population or an absolute solvation free energy.

multi_mlip_admission_gate.important_cancellation: A size-extensive target MLIP atomic-energy zero can cancel in the atom-conserving A(S)n - (S)n - A cycle. This does not validate intermolecular forces, sampling overlap, thermochemistry, or the outer-continuum treatment.
multi_mlip_admission_gate.measured_cost_comparator: end-to-end wall time and target evaluations versus the corresponding MM implicit or explicit reference workflow, not only the continuum correction kernel

overall_decision.reason: QCG is the strongest complete upstream thermodynamic scaffold and FEBISS is a useful site-selection preprocessor, but neither supplies a validated arbitrary-gas-MLIP neutral aqueous product route. Current QCG is wired directly to xTB/GFN-family growth, sampling, optimization, and frequencies; FEBISS begins from an external explicit trajectory and does not compute the complete transfer free energy. Route 1 therefore retains the prebuilt engineering mode, adds no automatic generator or FreeSolv selector, and keeps the target-MLIP proposal/reweighting cycle as research-only until every compatibility, overlap, thermodynamic, accuracy, and cost gate passes.
revisit_only_if: a maintained upstream exposes the full QCG-like cycle to arbitrary target energy/gradient/Hessian backends or a separately reviewed adapter does so without forking scientific logic
each admitted MLIP is validated for solute-solvent and pure-solvent clusters, not only isolated gas molecules
target/reference overlap and cluster-size/conformer convergence fail closed with uncertainty
a prospectively frozen neutral aqueous benchmark materially improves Route 1 accuracy
end-to-end multi-MLIP cost is measured against a like-for-like MM workflow

protocol.admission_rule: An automatic product path requires a closed thermodynamic cycle, a maintained upstream or a separately justified implementation boundary, target-MLIP validity for every cycle species, overlap and ensemble convergence, a prospective neutral aqueous accuracy gate, and measured multi-MLIP cost. A shell generator or fixed-shell potential alone is insufficient.
steps: separate a fixed-shell configurational potential from an absolute transfer free energy
enumerate every cluster, pure-solvent, standard-state, and ensemble term
audit CREST QCG documentation and current source for arbitrary-backend connectivity
audit FEBISS source scope as a possible inner-shell proposal generator
check whether the published evidence validates neutral aqueous small molecules and arbitrary MLIPs
record a fail-closed product decision without adding a paper-derived runtime
generate solute-solvent and pure-solvent proposal ensembles with a maintained tool such as QCG
evaluate every atom-conserving cycle state with one target MLIP plus one audited outer fixed-charge provider
use reference-to-target MBAR or nonequilibrium switching only when overlap diagnostics pass
include thermochemical or rigorously sampled free-energy contributions and explicit standard states
average over conformers, coordination states, and cluster sizes with uncertainty
validate prospectively on neutral aqueous molecules for each admitted MLIP compatibility class
measure total cost against a like-for-like MM workflow
research_only_path_if_reopened.why_not_current_product: No current upstream performs this end-to-end arbitrary-MLIP cycle, the available Route 1 runtime supplies only one fixed-shell potential, and no neutral FreeSolv accuracy/cost evidence closes the product gates.
